prompt_text: I am planning a trip. Should I book on Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com, and how do I find a good host?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: it depends on what you value. All three are legitimate — choose by property type, flexibility, fees and how much vetting you want to do. Below I’ll summarize differences, give practical tips for finding a trustworthy host, a vetting checklist, safety warnings, and a short message template you can send to hosts.

Platform comparison (quick pros & cons)
- Airbnb
  - Pros: widest variety (private rooms, shared, whole homes), strong host profiles and ratings, good filters (self-check-in, family-friendly, work-ready), “Superhost” badge, flexible monthly-stays options.
  - Cons: service and cleaning fees can add up; some listings are managed by professional hosts, others by individuals; cancellation policies vary widely.
- Vrbo
  - Pros: focused on whole-home/vacation properties (good for families/groups), strong search for entire houses, often fewer shared-space surprises.
  - Cons: similar extra fees (cleaning/service); fewer private-room options; host badges vary by market.
- Booking.com
  - Pros: huge inventory including hotels + apartments, lots of instant-book options, often easier refundable/cancellation terms, widely used by travelers who want immediate confirmation.
  - Cons: some short-term rentals are managed by agencies rather than individual hosts (less direct host relationship), host details sometimes minimal, review style more hotel-like.

Which to pick
- Want a whole house for a family/group: Vrbo (or Airbnb whole-home filters).
- Want unusual stays, private rooms, experiences, or monthly discounts: Airbnb.
- Want instant booking, hotel-style cancellation options, or last-minute flexibility: Booking.com.
- Price/availability: check all three and compare total price breakdown (cleaning, service, taxes) for the same dates.

How to find a good host — step-by-step
1. Set non-negotiables first: dates, budget (total, not nightly), area, number of beds/bathrooms, parking, Wi‑Fi, pet/child rules.
2. Use filters: entire place vs private room, Instant Book vs request, amenities (kitchen, washer, AC), self check-in, free cancellation.
3. Sort & compare: sort by “reviews” or “recommended” and check total price (not just nightly).
4. Read recent reviews: focus on reviews from the last 12–24 months for accuracy (hosts and neighborhoods change).
5. Look at host profile and response metrics: response rate/time and how many stays/years hosting. Bad sign = very few reviews and no profile or no verified ID.
6. Check calendar behavior: wide availability with many last-minute bookings can be OK; an always-open calendar with low bookings + new listing needs more vetting.
7. Inspect the listing closely: clear photos, detailed description, complete amenities list, house rules, deposit policy, check-in instructions.
8. Contact the host before booking: ask clarifying questions (see sample below). Good hosts reply promptly with clear answers.
9. Confirm logistics: exact check-in method, where keys are, emergency contact, parking, nearest transport/grocery.
10. Beware of red flags: requests to pay outside the platform, inconsistent photos or copy/paste descriptions across listings, host avoids questions, many one-word or generic reviews.

Vetting checklist (quick, printable)
- Recent reviews (within 12 months): yes/no
- Overall rating: 4.7+ (or read context)
- Number of reviews: many vs few — many is safer
- Host response rate/time: high and fast
- Verified ID or platform verification: yes
- Clear calendar & pricing breakdown: yes
- House rules & cancellation policy acceptable: yes
- Photos match description and show actual beds/bathroom/kitchen: yes
- Self-check-in or explicit check-in instructions: yes
- Emergency contact/local manager available: yes

Key questions to ask a host (send before booking if unsure)
- Is the address exact? If not, how close is it to [landmark/neighborhood]?
- How does check-in work (keybox, host meeting, keypad)? Can late check-in be arranged?
- Are there any ongoing renovations or noisy neighbors expected on our dates?
- Where do we park, and is parking included or free on the street?
- Is Wi‑Fi speed suitable for remote work? (ask for Mbps if you need reliable video calls)
- Are linens, towels, and basic kitchen essentials provided?
- What is your cancellation / refund policy for unexpected changes?
- Who do we contact in an emergency or for maintenance during our stay?

Sample short message to send a host
Hi [Host name], I’m [first name] and I’m planning a stay from [date]–[date] with [# guests, adults/children]. I like your listing — quick questions: how does check-in work, is parking included, and is the Wi‑Fi reliable for video calls? Also, are there any house rules I should know about? Thank you — I look forward to hearing from you.  

Safety & fraud prevention
- Never pay off-platform. Book and pay only through Airbnb/Vrbo/Booking.com.
- Do a reverse image search on suspicious photos.
- Be wary of listings with unusually low prices for a popular area.
- Keep all communication on the platform so there’s a record if problems arise.
- Confirm smoke detectors, locks, and basic safety items are present.
- For new/unreviewed hosts: insist on more photos, verify ID and responsiveness before booking.

Other practical tips
- Check the total price before booking — fees/taxes often add 20–40% to the nightly rate.
- For long stays, ask about discounts and utilities included.
- If you need quiet or strict check-in times, prefer hosts with explicit self-check-in instructions.
- If traveling for work, filter for “work ready” or confirm a workspace and reliable internet.
- If you’re risk-averse, prefer listings with free cancellation or book through Booking.com where many options offer flexible cancellation.

If you tell me your destination, dates, trip type (couple/family/business), and must-have amenities, I can:
- Recommend which platform is likely best for your needs
- Suggest search filters and keywords
- Draft a tailored message to send hosts or spot-check a few listings for you
